# Story 01 — Repo, ignore rules and branch conventions (Story: CRM-16)

## Prerequisites

- None. CRM-16 is the first story of the `platform` feature and of the whole backlog (see `scripts/backlog.txt` line 20: `STORY 1|repo-conventions|…|ALL:0:3|-|-`). It has no dependencies and blocks nothing directly, but every later story is cut from the `main` branch conventions this plan defines.
- Coordinate with nobody: the repository already exists on disk with the planning system (`.squad/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`) committed. This story **conventions** what is there; it does not re-create it.

---

## Story Goal

Turn the existing repo into a repo that has an obvious shape and obvious rules **before** any application code is written into it. After this story:

1. There is one git repository at the root, containing three currently-empty application roots (`api/`, `web/`, `android/`) that are visible in a fresh clone.
2. `.gitignore` ignores **by shape** (patterns), never by hand-typed filenames, so a new private note in the root never has to be added to it.
3. `README.md` at the root describes what the repository **is today** — three empty roots plus the planning system — with **no roadmap**, **no sprint numbers**, **no mention of AI assistance**, and **no future-tense promises**.
4. `docs/git.md` documents the **branch model** (`main`, `sprint-N`, `<ID>-<slug>` story branches, tag per closed sprint, merged branches deleted) and the **commit style** (subject = what changed; body = why and what alternative was rejected).
5. Every commit produced on the story branch reads as a record of decisions, not "wip".

**Not in scope:** any application code in `api/`, `web/`, `android/` (no Express, no React, no Gradle); CI (that is `PLATFORM-13-ALL` / CRM-28); the structure-rules script (`PLATFORM-15-ALL` / CRM-30); DB schema and seed (`PLATFORM-2-API` / `PLATFORM-8-API`, CRM-17/23); any change to the backlog system under `scripts/`.

## Product rules (from story)

**Current behaviour** (before this story)

- Repository exists with commits under `.squad/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`. `.gitignore` exists at the root and already matches most of the acceptance list (see file inventory above).
- No `README.md` at the repository root.
- No `docs/git.md`.
- `api/`, `web/`, `android/` exist as empty directories on disk but carry no tracked file, so a fresh `git clone` **does not create them**.

**New behaviour** (after this story)

- **One repository, three roots.** `api/`, `web/`, `android/` are each visible in a fresh clone because each contains one tracked placeholder file (`.gitkeep`).
- **`.gitignore` ignores by shape, never by name.** The whitelist is exactly the acceptance list, and every rule is a pattern. A new private root-level markdown note (`ideas.md`, `todo.md`, `scratch.md`) is ignored automatically by the `/*.md` + `!/README.md` pair — nobody edits `.gitignore` when they add a note.
- **`README.md` at the root exists and is present-tense.** It names the three roots, describes the planning system in `.squad/`, `docs/`, and `scripts/`, and states nothing about upcoming sprints, roadmap milestones, features that do not yet exist, or AI tooling.
- **`docs/git.md` exists** and defines:
  - Long-lived branches: `main` only.
  - Sprint branches: `sprint-N` cut from `main`, merged back to `main` at the end of the sprint; a tag `sprint-N` (or the equivalent `block-N`, per the workspace's own vocabulary in `docs/taxonomy.md` line 109) is placed on the merge commit.
  - Story branches: `<ID>-<slug>` (for this story: `CRM-16-repo-conventions`), cut from the current sprint branch, merged back into it, deleted on merge.
  - Commit style: subject line is imperative present-tense, ≤ 72 chars, says **what changed**. Body (blank line after subject) says **why** and **what alternative was rejected**. Wrap body at 72 columns.
  - **No AI attribution in any commit.** No `Co-authored-by: … noreply@anthropic.com`, no "Generated with", no `🤖` trailer. If a commit ends up with one, it is rewritten (`git commit --amend`, `git rebase -i`) **before** the branch is pushed for review.
- **`git log` on `CRM-16-repo-conventions`** reads as a sequence of decisions: one commit per acceptance-list item (or per group), each with a body explaining why this shape and not another.

## Implementation tasks

No backend, frontend or mobile code is added. Every change in this story is a documentation, ignore-rule, or placeholder change under the repository root and `docs/`.

### 1 — Verify and extend `.gitignore`

**File:** `.gitignore` (extend; do **not** rewrite)

Confirmed present after reading the file top to bottom:

- Line 2: `/*.md`
- Line 3: `!/README.md`
- Lines 5–8: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.gradle/`
- Lines 9–12: `local.properties`, `*.iml`, `.idea/`, `.DS_Store`
- Lines 13–15: `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`
- Lines 16–19: `api/*.db`, `api/*.db-journal`, `api/*.db-shm`, `api/*.db-wal`

Cross-check each against the acceptance list in the intake (lines 93–98). Every listed item is present. **Do not add or reorder anything** unless a listed item is genuinely missing on re-read.

If — and only if — an item is missing, append it to the bottom of the file under a single-line comment `# CRM-16 additions`. Never re-sort the existing block; the file's ordering carries prior decisions.

### 2 — Create the root `README.md`

**Create file:** `README.md` (at the repository root)

Constraints — this is what `.gitignore` line 3 whitelists, and its content must satisfy intake acceptance criterion at line 99:

- Present tense only. No "will", no "upcoming", no sprint numbers.
- No AI attribution — no "generated with", no "Claude", no "🤖".
- Names exactly three application roots (`api/`, `web/`, `android/`) and the planning system (`.squad/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`).
- Says the three roots are currently empty and will grow story by story; does **not** say what will land in which sprint.

Suggested skeleton (adjust wording, keep the sections):

```markdown
# Support Desk

One repository, three roots.

## The three roots

- `api/` — the JavaScript/Node HTTP service. Empty today.
- `web/` — the React client. Empty today.
- `android/` — the Kotlin mobile client. Empty today.

Each root has its own build, its own tests, and its own package manifest.
Each grows one story at a time.

## The planning system

- `.squad/` — the intake for each story, and the plan generated from it.
- `docs/` — the rules that outlive any one story (taxonomy, architecture,
  git conventions, block plan).
- `scripts/` — the backlog and the checks that read it.

## Where to start

Read, in order:

1. `docs/taxonomy.md` — what things are called.
2. `docs/architecture.md` — where code goes.
3. `docs/git.md` — how branches, tags and commits work.
```

Do **not** add "Getting started" instructions for `npm install`, `./gradlew`, etc. — none of the roots is runnable yet, and a false instruction is worse than a missing one. `PLATFORM-19-ALL` (hardening, CRM-34) is the story that adds runnable instructions once they exist (see `scripts/criteria/platform.md` lines 236–245).

### 3 — Create `docs/git.md`

**Create file:** `docs/git.md`

Sections, in this order:

1. **One repository, three roots.** One sentence naming `api/`, `web/`, `android/` and pointing at `docs/architecture.md` for the internal shape.
2. **Branches.**
   - `main` — always green, always deployable-in-principle. Nothing is pushed directly to `main` except the merge commit at the end of a sprint.
   - `sprint-N` — cut from `main` at the start of sprint N. All story branches for sprint N are cut from and merged into `sprint-N`. Merged back into `main` at the end of the sprint. Tagged `sprint-N` on the merge commit. (Note: the taxonomy calls this a **block**; the two words mean the same thing. Branch names and tags use `sprint-N` because that is what the tracker labels use — see `scripts/backlog.txt` line 4.)
   - `<ID>-<slug>` — story branch. Example: `CRM-16-repo-conventions`. Cut from the current sprint branch, merged back into it, **deleted on merge** (both locally and on the remote).
3. **Tags.** One per closed sprint. Format `sprint-N`. Placed on the sprint's merge commit into `main`.
4. **Commit style.**
   - Subject: imperative, present-tense, ≤ 72 chars, no trailing period. Says **what changed**.
   - Body: separated from subject by a blank line, wrapped at 72 columns. Says **why** this change and **what alternative was rejected**. Every non-trivial commit has a body.
   - **No AI trailers.** No `Co-authored-by: … noreply@anthropic.com`, no `🤖 Generated with …`, no other mention of AI tooling. If one slips in, it is removed with `git commit --amend` (last commit) or `git rebase -i <ref>` (older commits) **before** the branch is pushed for review.
5. **A short worked example** showing one story branch's log — three or four commits, each with a one-sentence subject and a two-line body — so a reader can see what "reads as a record of decisions" means.

### 4 — Make the three roots visible in a fresh clone

**Create file:** `api/.gitkeep` (empty)
**Create file:** `web/.gitkeep` (empty)
**Create file:** `android/.gitkeep` (empty)

`.gitkeep` is a convention, not a git feature; the empty file is what makes git track the directory. One placeholder per root, and nothing else. Do not add a README inside each root — the root-level `README.md` names the roots, and adding a per-root README now would restate that in three places (which `docs/taxonomy.md` line 130 forbids: "no document restates another document").

If `/*.md` in `.gitignore` (line 2) would ignore a per-root README, that is another reason not to add one; `.gitkeep` is not markdown and is not ignored.

### 5 — Shape the commits on the story branch

`sprint-0` does not exist yet — this is the first story of the first sprint.
Bootstrap the model this story itself defines: `git checkout -b sprint-0 main`,
then cut the story branch from it: `git checkout -b CRM-16-repo-conventions sprint-0`.

Cut the branch and make one commit per acceptance-list item (or per small group). Suggested log — subjects only; each commit gets a body explaining the alternative rejected:

1. `docs: add root README naming the three roots and the planning system`
2. `chore: track empty api/, web/, android/ with .gitkeep`
3. `docs(git): document sprint and story branch model, commit style`
4. `chore(gitignore): (only if extended) note the added shape` — omit entirely if section 1 confirmed nothing was missing.

Each body answers **why this and not the alternative**. Example for commit 2:

> Track each empty root with `.gitkeep` rather than an empty per-root
> `README.md`. A per-root README would restate what the root README
> already says, and `/*.md` in `.gitignore` would ignore it anyway.
> `.gitkeep` is one byte and one convention.

Before push, run `git log --format='%B'` on the branch and confirm no line contains "Claude", "🤖", "Generated with", or an Anthropic email address. If any does, rewrite before pushing.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **A pre-existing commit already carries an AI trailer.** Trigger: any commit already on `main` or on a shared branch has a `Co-authored-by: … noreply@anthropic.com` line. Expected behaviour: **out of scope** for this story to rewrite history on `main` (that would rewrite `.squad/` and `docs/` commits everyone shares). Record the violation in `docs/git.md` as a **known deviation** with a one-line note. The rule "no AI attribution" is enforced strictly for commits made **from this story onward**.
- **`.gitignore` `/*.md` accidentally ignores a doc file added at the root.** Trigger: someone drops `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the root. Expected behaviour: it is ignored by design. Docs live under `docs/` (see `docs/architecture.md` and the file layout there). If a new root-level doc is genuinely wanted later, the rule is extended by adding one `!/CONTRIBUTING.md` line, not by removing `/*.md`. Note this in `docs/git.md` under commit style so the executor sees it.
- **Someone creates `README.md` inside `api/`, `web/`, or `android/`.** Trigger: reflex "every folder needs a README". Expected behaviour: `/*.md` at line 2 only matches the **root**, so the per-root README **is tracked** — which is exactly what this story does **not** want. `docs/git.md` names this explicitly: the three roots carry `.gitkeep`, not `README.md`, until `PLATFORM-19-ALL` (hardening, CRM-34) decides otherwise.
- **`api/*.db` patterns exist but the `api/` directory is empty.** Trigger: the acceptance list requires the pattern regardless. Expected behaviour: `.gitignore` lines 16–19 already carry them; keep them even though no `.db` file exists yet, so the first API story doesn't have to add them.
- **Branch name collision with tracker id casing.** Trigger: a story with a lowercase tracker id (`crm-16`). Expected behaviour: `docs/git.md` states branch names use the tracker id **verbatim as printed by the tracker** (`CRM-16-repo-conventions`), because git branch names are case-sensitive on Linux and case-insensitive on macOS, and mixed casing across sprints causes cross-platform breakage.
- **Merged story branch not deleted.** Trigger: reviewer forgets `git branch -d` after merge. Expected behaviour: `docs/git.md` names this as the rule; enforcement is by convention until `PLATFORM-13-ALL` (CI, CRM-28) automates it. Note in the doc that automated pruning is out of scope for this story.
- **A note file named `ai-notes.md` or `claude.md` at the root.** Trigger: developer takes AI-assisted notes locally. Expected behaviour: `/*.md` ignores it automatically — `.gitignore` does **not** name it, per the workspace-wide rule in the intake (lines 127–131). If it ever appears in `git status` as tracked, something is wrong with the ignore rules and must be investigated before merge.
- **`docs/git.md` disagreeing with `docs/taxonomy.md`.** Trigger: this story uses "sprint" and the taxonomy uses "block". Expected behaviour: one paragraph in `docs/git.md` states the equivalence with a link to `docs/taxonomy.md` line 102. `docs/verify-docs.mjs` (a future check under `PLATFORM-14-ALL` (CRM-29)) will refuse a broken cross-doc link; do not cite a line number in `taxonomy.md` that does not exist.

## Test Plan

This story ships no runnable code, so tests are **manual verification steps**. Do them in order and check each off in `## Done Criteria`.

1. **Fresh-clone shape.** In a scratch directory: `git clone <repo> shape-check && cd shape-check && ls -A api web android`. Expected: each of `api/.gitkeep`, `web/.gitkeep`, `android/.gitkeep` is listed. Nothing else in those directories.
2. **`.gitignore` — by shape, not by name.** In a fresh clone: `touch ideas.md scratch.md ai-notes.md && git status --porcelain`. Expected: **empty output** — all three are ignored by the `/*.md` line. Then `touch README.md-copy && git status --porcelain` — also empty. Then `git status --porcelain README.md` — README.md is tracked (or, if this is the create-README commit, untracked and about to be added).
3. **`.env` shape.** `touch .env .env.local .env.example && git status --porcelain`. Expected: only `.env.example` shows as untracked; `.env` and `.env.local` are ignored.
4. **`api/*.db` shape.** `touch api/support.db api/support.db-wal api/support.db-shm api/support.db-journal && git status --porcelain`. Expected: empty. Undo with `rm api/support.db*`.
5. **`docs/git.md` present and self-consistent.** `grep -n "sprint-N" docs/git.md` prints the branch section; `grep -n "block" docs/git.md` prints the one-line equivalence note; `grep -in "co-authored-by\|generated with\|claude\|🤖" docs/git.md` prints **nothing** — the doc names the rule but doesn't demonstrate it.
6. **`README.md` present-tense only.** `grep -inE "will|upcoming|roadmap|sprint [0-9]|block [0-9]" README.md` — expected: no matches. `grep -in "claude\|🤖\|generated with\|anthropic" README.md` — expected: no matches.
7. **`git log` reads as decisions.** `git log --format='%s%n%n%b%n---' CRM-16-repo-conventions ^main` prints each commit with subject and body. Expected: every commit body answers "why this and not the alternative"; no commit body is empty except possibly the `.gitkeep`-only commit; no line matches `grep -iE 'co-authored-by|generated with|claude|🤖'`.
8. **No AI attribution anywhere in the story branch.** `git log --format='%B' CRM-16-repo-conventions ^main | grep -iE 'co-authored-by|generated with|claude|🤖|anthropic'` — expected: empty output. If it prints anything, rewrite the offending commit(s) before pushing.

There is no automated test suite yet. `PLATFORM-13-ALL` (CI, CRM-28) and `PLATFORM-15-ALL` (structure checks, CRM-30) will later automate the equivalent of steps 2–8; do **not** add ad-hoc test scripts under `scripts/` in this story (that is the "no changes to the backlog system under `scripts/`" out-of-scope line in the intake).

## Migration / Rollback

Not applicable to source code, but note two irreversible-ish operations:

- **Adding tracked `.gitkeep` files.** Rollback is `git rm api/.gitkeep web/.gitkeep android/.gitkeep && git commit`. Trivial.
- **`docs/git.md` becomes the authority for branch naming.** Once merged, later stories cite this file. If the branch model is later changed, `docs/git.md` is **edited**, not deleted — the git tags from prior sprints remain valid.
- **Never rewrite history on `main`.** If a bad commit lands on `main` from this story, fix it forward with a new commit; do not `git push --force` `main`. This is stated in `docs/git.md` under commit style.

If the story branch is abandoned before merge: `git branch -D CRM-16-repo-conventions && git push origin --delete CRM-16-repo-conventions`. Nothing else is affected because no shared file outside the branch is created before merge.
